concept.name: Preliminary support
concept.definition: The Wyckoff event (PS) in which substantial buying first provides pronounced support after a prolonged decline, marked by widening price spread and increased volume that signal the downtrend may be approaching its end. It is an early warning, not a confirmed bottom.
concept.intuition: The first time in a long slide that buyers show up in force and noticeably slow the fall.
concept.mechanics: During a downtrend, the analyst watches for a down-bar sequence where volume and spread expand but downward progress slows; that buying interest is labeled preliminary support. PS typically precedes the selling climax and begins Phase A of an accumulation trading range.
concept.failure_modes: A single high-volume support day can be absorbed and the decline can continue; PS says nothing about how much further the market may fall before a final low.
concept.misconceptions: Preliminary support is not the bottom itself and does not warrant buying on its own; Wyckoff treats it as the first hint, with confirmation coming from the selling climax and secondary test that follow.
concept.example: After a 30% slide, a stock posts its heaviest volume day in months but closes well off the low; the analyst marks the bar as preliminary support and waits for climactic action.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
